questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chemolithotrophs are those bacteria which can utilize
options: Inorganic material as the energy source
Organic compound as the electron source
questions.solution: A chemolithotroph is an organism that is able to use inorganic reduced compounds as a source of energy. This mode of metabolism is known as chemolithotrophy. Other than chemolithotrophic the major autotrophic mode of nutrition is photoautotrophic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a plant-like protist?
questions.solution: Desmid, Dinoflagellate, and Diatom are the plant-like protists. Slime mould is a fungi-like protist.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Protistan genome has& & & & & &
options: Nucleoprotein in direct contact with cell substance
Gene containing nucleoproteins condensed together in loose mass
questions.solution: Protistans are eukaryotes with true nucleus and genetic material is embedded inside the nucleus. DNA is not naked and is found to be associated with histone protein.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In lichens, sexual reproduction belongs to
questions.solution: Lichens exhibit the symbiotic association between algae and fungi. The fungal partner is involved in sexual reproduction with the help of reproductive structures called apothecia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) genes are
questions.solution:
All viruses are nucleoprotein (Nucleic acid + Protein) in the structure. The nucleic acid (DNA and RNA) is the genetic material. In a particular virus, either DNA or RNA is genetic material; never both are present in a virus. Hence viruses are:

(i) Double-stranded DNA or ds DNA - Hepatitis B

(ii) Single-stranded DNA or ss DNA - Coliphage

(iii) Double-stranded RNA or ds RNA - Reovirus, wound Tumor virus

(iv) Single-stranded RNA or ss RNA - Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mycoplasmas are different from other prokaryotes by&
options: Presence of chitin in cell walls
Presence of murein in cell walls
Presence of proteins in cell walls
questions.solution: Mycoplasma is a wall-less bacteria. It is also known as PPLO. Because of the absence of a cell wall, it may have several shapes therefore termed as pleomorphic organisms. The absence of a cell wall makes them resistant to penicillin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Halophiles differ from eubacteria in
options: Having different cell wall and cell membrane structure
More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Halophiles& are organisms that thrive in high salt concentrations. They are a type of extremophile organisms. The name comes from the Greek word for "salt-loving", as they survive in extremely saline conditions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Scum floats on the surface of the water because
options: The density of cells is more than that of water
questions.solution: As many algal cells have gas vesicles which allow them to undergo vertical migration in the water column as a response to light conditions. Photosynthesis during day time causes the release of oxygen that makes their body buoyant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The wall of bacteria consists of
questions.solution: The bacterial cell wall contains peptidoglycan or mucopeptide or murein with diaminopimelic acid, lipid and protein. Chemically, peptidoglycan is composed of N-acetyl glucosamine (NAG) and N-acetyl muramic acid (NAM).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bacteria are present in which of the following kingdom?
questions.solution: Monera is a kingdom that contains unicellular organisms with a prokaryotic cell organization, such as bacteria. They are single-celled organisms with no true nuclear membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which type of organism are PPLO?
questions.solution: Mycoplasma is also known as pleuropneumonia like organisms (PPLO).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When fungi feed on dead organic matter, they are known as
questions.solution: All fungi are heterotrophs in their nutrition. Some depend upon organic matter known as saprophytes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following organisms possesses characteristics of both a plant and an animal?
questions.solution: Euglena is a connecting link between plant and animal as it shows mixotrophic nutrition. In the presence of sunlight, it carries out photosynthesis due to pigments present in it and in absence of sunlight it carries out holozoic nutrition and engulfs small particles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pseudopopdia are found in _____________ and help in________________.
questions.solution: Streaming of protoplasm in the unicellular organisms like Amoeba is a simple form of movement. Movement of cilia, flagella, and tentacles are shown by many organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Archaebacteria can survive better than other bacteria in unfavourable conditions because of their
questions.solution: The cell walls of archaebacteria are distinctive from those of eubacteria. Archaebacterial cell walls are composed of different polysaccharides and proteins, with no peptidoglycan. Many archaebacteria have cell walls made of the polysaccharide pseudomurein. The cell wall of archaea, as of any other prokaryote, is surrounding the cell outside the cytoplasmic membrane and is mediating the interaction with the environment. In this regard, it can be involved in cell shape maintenance, protection against virus, heat, acidity or alkalinity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the correct statement regarding retrovirus.
options: An RNA virus that can synthesize DNA during infection.
A DNA virus that can synthesize RNA during infection.
questions.solution:
Retrovirus, any of a group of viruses that belong to the family retroviridae and that characteristically carry their genetic blueprint in the form of ribonucleic acid (RNA). They have ssRNA as genetic material. It is a type of RNA virus that inserts a copy of its genome into the DNA of a host cell that it invades, thus changing the genome of that cell. It uses a special enzyme called reverse transcriptase to translate its genetic information into DNA.

That DNA can then integrate into the host cell's DNA. Once integrated, the virus can use the host cell's components to make additional viral particles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Most of the unicellular organisms are kept under
questions.solution: According to five kingdom classification, single cellular eukaryotes come under Protista and single cellular prokaryotes come under Monera. Thus all single unicellular organisms belong to these two groups.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct about Phycomycetes?
options: The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic.
A zygospore is formed by fusion of two gametes.
questions.solution: In the members of Phycomycetes, the mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic. Asexual reproduction takes place by zoospores (motile) or by aplanospores (non-motile). These spores are endogenously produced in the sporangium. A zygospore is formed by the fusion of two gametes. These gametes are similar in morphology (isogamous) or dissimilar (anisogamous or oogamous). Some common examples are Mucor, Rhizopus (the bread mould mentioned earlier), and Albugo (the parasitic fungi on mustard).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The smallest among the following is:
questions.solution: Bacteriophage is a virus that attacks bacterial cell. Bacteriophages are smaller than Tobacco mosaic virus which is a plant virus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The cellulosic cell wall is observed in members of
questions.solution: A plant cell wall is arranged in layers and contains cellulose microfibrils, hemicellulose, pectin, lignin, and soluble protein. These components are organized into three major layers: the primary cell wall, the middle lamella, and the secondary cell wall. Beside higher plants some members of protists are also having cellulosic cell wall.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Paramoecium and Plasmodium belong to the same kingdom as that of Penicillium
Lichen is a composite organism formed from the symbiotic association of an algae and a protozoan
Yeast used in making bread and beer is a fungus
questions.solution:
Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a yeast used in making bread (Baker's yeast) and commercial production of ethanol.

Paramoecium and Plasmodium belong to the animal kingdom while penicillium is a fungus. Lichen is a composite organism formed from the symbiotic association of algae and a fungus. Nostoc and Anabaena are examples of kingdom Monera.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following feature of halophiles, is used to differentiate them from eubacteria?
options: Having different cell wall and cell membrane structure.
questions.solution: Halophiles, the name comes from the Greek word for "salt-loving," are a special type of bacteria that live in some of the harshest habitats such as extreme salty areas. These bacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The causal organism for African sleeping sickness is&
questions.solution: African sleeping sickness disease also called trypanosomiasis common in Africa is caused by parasite Trypanosoma gambiense. The parasite is transmitted by Tes-Tse fly (Glossina palpalis).&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is an edible fungus?
questions.solution: The fructifications of certain fungi are used as nutritious and delicious food e.g., Agaricus bisporus and A. campestris (mushrooms).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Dikaryon formation is characteristics of
questions.solution: The formation of secondary mycelium is the feature of Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes. A secondary mycelium forms upon conjugation of two sexually compatible hyphae. The secondary mycelium is dikaryotic, in that it has two haploid nuclei, one from each parent. As the dikaryotic mycelium grows, the cells divide and more septa are formed between the new cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: Cyanobacteria form mycorrhizae which helps in the absorption of phosphate
The genome of TMV is RNA.
questions.solution: "Myco" - "rhiza" literally means "fungus" - "root" and describes the mutually beneficial relationship between the plant and root fungus. These specialized fungi colonize plant roots in a symbiotic manner and extend far into the soil. Mycorrhizal fungal filaments in the soil are truly extensions of root systems and are more effective in nutrient and water absorption than the roots themselves. Cyanobacteria on the other hand is not a fungus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which class of fungi, asexual spores are produced exogenously, while sexual spores are produced endogenously?
questions.solution: In ascomycetes,& the asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on the special mycelium called conidiophores. Conidia on germination produce mycelium. Sexual spores are called ascospores which are produced endogenously in sac-like asci (singular ascus). These asci are arranged in different types of fruiting bodies called ascocarps.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many organisms in the list given below are autotrophs?
Lactobacillus, Nostoc, Chara, Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter, Streptomyces, Saccharomyces, Trypanosoma, Porphyra, Wolffia.
questions.solution:
Autotrophic nutrition involves the manufacture of organic materials from inorganic raw materials with the help of energy obtained from outside sources. It is of two types chemosynthesis and photosynthesis.
Chemosynthetic: The organisms which are able to manufacture their organic food from inorganic raw materials with the help of energy derived from exergonic chemical reactions are called chemoautotrophs. Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are chemoautotrophic nitrifying bacteria.
Photosynthetic: Those organisms who can manufacture organic compounds from inorganic raw materials with the help of solar energy in the presence of photosynthetic pigments chlorophyll a, carotenoids and phycobilins. Chara is a green alga having chlorophyll a, b, carotenes and xanthophylls. Porphyra is a red alga containing chlorophyll a, carotenoids and phycobilins and Wolffia is an aquatic angiosperm which consists of photosynthetic pigments, chlorophyll a, b, carotenoids and xanthophylls.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which bacteria is utilized in gober gas plants?
questions.solution: Methanobacillus (methanogen) occurs in marshes and also in dung. It produces CH_{4} gas under anaerobic condition and is utilised in gobar gas plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In some prokaryotes like ____________, there are other membranous extensions in the cytoplasm called _________ which contain pigments.
questions.solution: In some prokaryotes like cyanobacteria, there are other membranous extensions into the cytoplasm called chromatophores which contain pigments.& Heterocyst is specialized cells present in some cyanobacteria which carries nitrogen fixation. They contain enzyme nitrogenase by which they carry out nitrogen fixation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the correct sequence of stages involved in the reproductive cycle of fungi.
questions.solution:
The reproductive cycle of fungi includes the following stages: Plasmogamy - Fusion of two motile or non-motile gametes.
Karyogamy - Fusion of two gamete nuclei.
Zygotic meiosis - This process results in the formation of haploid spores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Lichens are ecologically important as they
options: Are symbionts of algae and fungi
questions.solution: Lichens play the role of pioneer species in primary succession on rocks. Lichens secrete acids to dissolve rocks and thus help in weathering and soil formation. Later on lichens make favourable conditions for the growth of very small plants like bryophytes, which are able to hold small amount of soil. Lichens are also SO_{2} pollution indicators.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria produce ATP by&
questions.solution: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidise various inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites and ammonia and use the released energy for their ATP production. They play a great role in recycling nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorous, iron and sulphur.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not true for retroviruses?
options: DNA is not present at any stage in the life cycle of retroviruses
Retroviruses carry gene for RNA - dependent DNA polymerase
The genetic material in mature retroviruses is RNA
Retroviruses are causative agents for certain kinds of cancer in man
questions.solution: Retroviruses have RNA as the genetic material and hence they exhibit reverse transcription where by DNA is synthesised on RNA template. They have reverse transcriptase as the enzyme.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The nitrogen-fixing bacteria Rhizobium is ________________ in nature.
questions.solution: Heterotrophic bacteria are the most abundant in nature. The majority are important decomposers. Many of them have a significant impact on human affairs. They are helpful in making curd from milk, production of antibiotics, fixing nitrogen in legume roots like Rhizobium, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Zygospore is formed from
questions.solution: Gametangial copulation involves direct conjugation (fusion) of two gametangia of opposite strain to form zygospore, e.g., Rhizopus, yeasts, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The nuclear membrane is absent in
questions.solution: Nostoc is prokaryote while rest are eukaryotes. The nuclear membrane is absent in prokaryotes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the structures are found in photosynthetic prokaryotes?

I. Mesosomes
II. Cellulose wall
III. Ribosomes
IV. Chloroplasts
questions.solution: Photosynthetic prokaryotes have their photosynthetic pigment in specialised infoldings of the plasma membrane called mesosomes. The cell wall of prokaryotes is made up of peptidoglycans. Cellulose cell wall and chloroplasts are present in plants which are eukaryotic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Heterocysts in Nostoc
options: are green cells capable of nitrogen fixation
questions.solution: Heterocysts in Nostoc& are large clear cells without chlorophyll. They have enzyme nitrogenase which helps in nitrogen fixation. In Nostoc, they are not situated terminally (at the ends) but are interspersed between the photosynthetic cells. Since they are clear, they are also called hyaline cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these combinations is correct about protozoans?
questions.solution: Entamoeba is an intestinal parasite in humans and is a part of amoeboid protozoans. Plasmodium causes malaria and is a sporozoan since it has a spore-like infective stage in its life cycle. Trypanosoma which causes sleeping sickness has flagella, and hence, it is a flagellated protozoan. Paramecium is an aquatic, actively moving organism because of the presence of thousands of cilia. Hence, it is a ciliated protozoan.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these fungi does not have a branched and septate mycelium?
questions.solution: Branched and septate mycelium is found in Ascomycetes (sac fungi), Basidiomycetes (club fungi), and Deuteromycetes (imperfect fungi). The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic in Phycomycetes. Neurospora belongs to Ascomycetes, Ustilago belongs to Basidiomycetes, Colletotrichum belongs to Deuteromycetes and Albugo, a parasitic fungus on mustard, belongs to Phycomycetes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The smallest disease-causing agent is ________, and it is made up of ___________
questions.solution: Prions are discovered by Prusiner in 1982. They are the smallest infectious protein particles which lack nucleic acid. Prions are modified hydrophobic glycoproteins that are resistant to protease action compared with normal proteins; they function as infectious agents. Prions change normal proteins to an infectious form, and they are found to& cause diseases in animals and not in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Term "virion'' is used for
questions.solution: Viruses lack cellular organization, they can survive only inside living host cell thus are called an obligate intracellular parasite, they cannot be cultured in an artificial medium.& A virion is an agent that infects living organisms, often causing disease.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the option having the fungi which belong to the same class
questions.solution: Rhizopus and Mucor are members of Phycomycetes. Aspergillus, Saccharomyces (yeast), Morchella (morels) are Ascomycetes fungi. Agaricus (Mushroom) contains edible Basidiomycetes fungi. Morchella, commonly called as morels, are edible Ascomycetes fungi.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the function of the rich protein layer found in Euglena instead of a cell wall?
options: It allows the organism to be heterotrophic in the absence of sunlight.
questions.solution: Euglenoids are freshwater organisms. Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible. They have two flagella, a short and a long one. Though they are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight, when deprived of sunlight, they behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the organism given below?
options: This organism has a cell wall made up of a protein called a pellicle.
It is both phototrophic and heterotrophic in nature.
Toxins released by them may even kill other marine animals such as& fish.
questions.solution: These organisms are mostly marine and photosynthetic. They appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells. The cell wall has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface. Most of them have two flagella, one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates. Very often, red dinoflagellates (example: Gonyaulax) undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides). Toxins released by such large numbers may even kill other marine animals such as fishes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Basidiomycetes, meiosis will take place in
questions.solution: Basidium is a club-shaped structure. Karyogamy and meiosis both will occur in basidium, and four basidiospores will form.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following can be used in the filtration of oils and syrups?
questions.solution: In diatoms, the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soapbox. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible. Thus, diatoms have left behind large amounts of cell wall deposits in their habitat; this accumulation over billions of years is referred to as ‘diatomaceous earth’. Being gritty, this soil is used in polishing and filtration of oils and syrups.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the light of recent classification of living organisms into three domains of life (bacteria, archaea, and eukarya), which one of the following statements is true about archaea?
options: Archaea resemble eukarya in all respects
Archaea have some novel features that are absent in other prokaryotes and eukaryotes
Archaea completely differ from both prokaryotes and eukaryotess
questions.solution: A domain of prokaryotic organisms containing the archaebacteria includes the methanogens which produce methane, the thermoacidophilic bacteria which live in an extremely hot and acidic environment and the halophilic bacteria which can only function at high salt concentrations and are abundant in the oceans.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Majority of plant viruses are transmitted by ________
questions.solution: Most of the plant viruses depend on a particular vector for transmission and for further spreading of the infection. Most significantly used vectors are piercing–sucking insects that easily transmit plant viruses.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Complete the analogy

Humans: DNA:: Viroids:: ?
questions.solution: DNA is the genetic material in humans. T.O. Diener discovered a new infectious agent called viroids. It was smaller than viruses and caused potato spindle tuber disease. It has free low molecular weight RNA but does not have a protein coat. Thus, the genetic material in viroids is RNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Oxygenic photosynthesis occurs in
questions.solution: Oscillatoria is a filamentous Gram-ve cyanobacteria which performs oxygenic photosynthesis because of the presence of chlorophyll-a like eukaryotic algae and higher plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Citrus canker is caused by
questions.solution: Some bacteria are pathogens causing damage to human beings, crops, farm animals and pets. Cholera, typhoid, tetanus, citrus canker are well-known diseases caused by different bacteria. Citrus canker is a disease affecting Citrus species and is caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas axonopodis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chlamydomonas and Chlorella were categorized under which kingdom in the five-kingdom classification?
questions.solution: Chlamydomonas and Chlorella, both can be categorized under the kingdom Protista, as they both follow the definition of a Protista, i.e., they are unicellular eukaryotes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following, asexual spores are generally not seen, but there is the development of a dikaryophase stage?
questions.solution:
When a fungus reproduces sexually, two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types come together and fuse.

In ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, the fusion of two haploid cells forms an intermediate stage called the dikaryotic stage. In this stage, one cell has two diploid nuclei. This stage is called dikaryophase. Later, the parental nuclei fuse, and the cells become diploid. Asexual spores are generally not seen in basidiomycetes, and they generally undergo fragmentation. Thus, basidiomycetes is the group in which asexual spores are generally not seen but dikaryophase is seen. Albugo belongs to phycomycetes, Claviceps belongs to ascomycetes, Alternaria belongs to deuteromycetes, and Agaricus (mushroom) belongs to basidiomycetes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding Deuteromycetes?

$I.$ Deuteromycetes are called perfect fungi.

$II.$ Members of Deuteromycetes were often moved to ascomycetes or basidiomycetes once their sexual stages were studied.

$III.$ Large number of Deuteromycetes are decomposers that help in nutrient cycling.

$IV.$ Their mycelium is aseptate and unbranched.
questions.solution: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi. The mode of sexual reproduction is not known in them. Once sexual stages of members of deuteromycetes were discovered they were often moved to ascomycetes and basidiomycetes. The members of deuteromycetes have septate and branched hyphae. Some members are saprophytes or parasites while a large number of them are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling. Some examples are Alternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Beijernick concluded that the cause of tobacco mosaic disease was not a filtrate toxin because
options: the infectious agent could not be cultivated on nutrient media
the infectious agent could be crystallized
the infectious agent reproduced and could be passed on from a plant infected with filtered sap
the sap was infectious even though it was& filtered to remove bacterias.
questions.solution: M.W. Beijerinek demonstrated that the extract of the infected plants of tobacco could cause infection in healthy plants and called the fluid as contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid). The virus was found to be smaller than bacteria because they passed through a bacteria proof filter.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Rust and smut disease of fungi are caused by fungi belonging to
options:
Rust Smut & Ascomycetes
Puccinia Ustilago

Smut Rust & Basidiomycetes
Puccinia Ustilago

Rust Smut & Basidiomycetes
Puccinia Ustilago

Smut Rust & Ascomycetes
Puccinia Ustilago
questions.solution: Rust of wheat is caused by Puccinia and smut is caused by Ustilago. Both are basidiomycetes fungi, and they are parasites on living plant body.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Read the following statements about golden algae and select the one which is false.
options: They have autotrophic mode of nutrition
questions.solution: Chrysophytes include diatoms and golden algae (desmids). They are found in freshwater as well as in marine environments. They are unicellular and eukaryotic and are included kingdom Protista. They are photosynthetic and can produce their own food.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The main difference in Gram $\text{+ve}$ and Gram $\text{-ve}$& bacteria resides in their
questions.solution: Bacteria can be classified into two groups on the basis of the differences in the cell envelopes and the manner in which they respond to the staining procedure developed by Christian Gram. Gram staining is a differential staining method that separates bacteria into two categories based on the cell wall composition. Those that take up the Gram stain are called Gram-positive and the other that does not takes up Gram stain are called Gram-negative bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: LSD is extracted from
questions.solution: Lysergic acid diethylamide is isolated from ergot caused by fungi Claviceps. Claviceps is an Ascomycetes fungus which causes ergot diseases in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: According to the three domain classification, Methanococcus and Rhizobium belong to
questions.solution: The three-domain system proposed by Carl Woese divides Kingdom Monera into two domains on the basis of differences in 16S rRNA genes: Archaea and Bacteria. The third domain is Eukaryota which has all eukaryotes. Also, there are 6 kingdoms- Archaebacteria in domain Archaea, Eubacteria in domain Bacteria and Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia in the domain Eukaryota. Methanococcus lies in Archaebacteria in domain Archaea and Rhizobium lies in Eubacteria in domain Bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct option for the given diagram.
questions.solution: Citrus canker is a bacterial disease caused in the citrus plants by Xanthomonas citri. In this brown corky, rings appear on leaves and fruits.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Observe given figure and identify with name and labelled $\text{A and B}$.
questions.solution: Nostoc, the genus of blue-green algae with cells arranged in beadlike chains that are grouped together in a gelatinous mass. Reproduction is by fragmentation. A special thick-walled cell has the ability to withstand desiccation for long periods of time. Like most blue-green algae, Nostoc contains two pigments, blue phycocyanin and red phycoerythrin, as well as chlorophyll, and has the ability to fix nitrogen in specialized cells called heterocysts.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The incipient nucleus is present in
questions.solution: Cyanobacteria belong to myxophyceae and are also known as blue-green algae. They are photosynthetic organisms having chlorophyll similar to higher plants. Unlike other bacteria, they carry out oxygenic photosynthesis as they are capable of utilizing water as a source of hydrogen in photosynthesis.& These cyanobacteria consist of& an incipient nucleus, which is a nucleoid or primitive nucleus dispersed in the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the correct option by analyzing the following statements.

(a) Aristotle classified plants into herbs, shrubs and trees on the basis of morphology.
(b) Two-kingdom classification by Linnaeus was based on the presence or absence of a cell wall.
(c) R.H. Whittaker included heterotrophic and chitinous-cell-wall-containing organisms in animals.

&
questions.solution:
Aristotle was the first to attempt a more scientific basis for classification. He used simple morphological characters to classify plants into trees, shrubs and herbs. He also divided animals into two groups; those which had red blood and those that did not. In Linnaeus' time, a two-kingdom system of classification with Plantae and Animalia kingdoms was developed that included all plants and animals, respectively. This system did not distinguish between the eukaryotes and prokaryotes, unicellular and multicellular organisms and photosynthetic (green algae) and non-photosynthetic (fungi) organisms.
R.H. Whittaker included heterotrophic and chitinous-cell-wall-containing organisms in a separate kingdom Fungi.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following scientist's contributions to viruses is correctly matched?

I. M.W. Beijerinek demonstrated that the extract of the infected plants of tobacco mosaic could cause infection in healthy plants and called the fluid as contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid).
II. W.M. Stanley showed that viruses could be crystallized and crystals consist largely of proteins.
III. The name virus that means venom or poisonous fluid was given by Dmitri Ivanowsky.
questions.solution: The name virus, that means venom or poisonous fluid, was given by Dmitri Ivanowsky (1892). He recognized certain microbes as the causal organisms of the mosaic disease of tobacco. These were found to be smaller than bacteria because they passed through bacteria-proof filters. M.W. Beijerinek (1898) demonstrated that the extract of the infected plants of tobacco could cause infection in healthy plants and called the fluid as contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid). W.M. Stanley (1935) showed that viruses could be crystallized and crystals consist largely of proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following statement/s is/are not the characteristic feature of Kingdom Protista?

$( a )$ They include chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime molds, and protozoans
$( b )$ Chief producers in the ocean are diatoms.
$( c )$ Toxins are released by some of the members of this kingdom.
$( d )$ They are either unicellular or multicellular.
questions.solution: All single-celled eukaryotes are placed under Protista, but the boundaries of this kingdom are not well-defined. What may be 'a photosynthetic protistan' to one biologist may be 'a plant' to others. Chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime moulds and protozoans are included under Protista. Members of Protista are primarily aquatic. Diatoms are chief producers of the ocean, and dinoflagellates are known to release some toxic substances.

questions.solution: The main aim of classification is to group similar organisms together. In the five-kingdom classification given by Whittaker, prokaryotes are separated from eukaryotes and fungi, which were earlier placed in the plant kingdom, were placed in a separate kingdom as they are saprophytes. However, viruses that are non-cellular have not been given any place in this classification. Also, all unicellular eukaryotes having diverse properties have been placed under the kingdom Protista. They contain autotrophic, heterotrophic and saprophytic protists. This is a demerit of this system.

This phenomenon is known as sporulation.

questions.solution: Whittaker has given the famous Five- Kingdom Classification. According to this classification the five kingdoms are Kingdom Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia. These kingdoms are divided on the basis of Number of cells, Cell type, Cell wall, Mode of nutrition and Ecological role. All these are characters of living cell. Viruses did not get any place in this kingdom because these are not considered as 'true living'. Viruses do not have cell organelles and hence do not carry metabolism and cannot exist independently. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Filament, hook and basal body are the parts of
options: Flagella in both eukaryotes and prokaryotes
questions.solution: Motility in Bacteria is due to presence of thin extensions called as Flagella. The number and arrangement of flagella varies in different types of bacteria. Flagella is made up of three main parts: Filament: Longest and main part that extends from cell surface to the outside and is composed of flagellin protein. Hook: Structure near the cell surface. Basal body: A system of rings embedded in cell envelope. The eukaryotes also possess flagella but these are structurally different from that of the prokaryotic flagella. Their core called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis. The axoneme usually has nine pairs of doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules. Such an arrangement of axonemal microtubules is referred to as the 9+2 array. The central tubules are connected by bridges and is also enclosed by a central sheath, which is connected to one of the tubules of each peripheral doublets by a radial spoke. Thus, there are nine radial spokes. The peripheral doublets are also interconnected by linkers.

questions.q: Free RNA as infectious particle and of low molecular weight
options: is a pathogen of both plants and animals
was discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971
questions.solution:
Viroids are the smallest infectious pathogens known, consisting solely of short strands of circular, single-stranded RNA without protein coats. They are mostly plant pathogens, some of which are of economical importance. Viroid genomes are extremely small in size, ranging from 246 to 467 nucleobases. In comparison, the genome of the smallest known viruses capable of causing an infection by themselves are around 2,000 nucleobases in size. The human pathogen hepatitis D virus is a defective RNA virus similar to viroids.

Viroids, the first known representatives of a new domain of "sub-viral pathogens," were discovered, initially characterized, and named by Theodor Otto Diener, plant pathologist at the U.S Department of Agriculture's Research Center in Beltsville, Maryland, in 1971. The first viroid to be identified was Potato spindle tuber viroid (PSTVd). Some 33 species have been identified.

The sequence of events in the fungal sexual cycle is plasmogamy, karyogamy, and then meiosis. In plasmogamy, the cytoplasm of two cells fuses with each other. In karyogamy, nuclei of two cells fuse with each other result in the formation of the zygote that will be diploid. After the formation of the zygote, meiosis occurs. questions.q: In some fungi such as _____, the fusion of two haploid cells immediately results in diploid cell while in other group of fungi like _____, an intervening dikaryotic stage occurs, called dikaryophase.
questions.solution:
In Fungi, sexual reproduction occurs by formation and fusion of two gametes with their nuclei. This type of reproduction is absent in the fungi group - Deuteromycetes.

In Sexual reproduction, the there is fusion of the nuclei as well as the cytoplasm. The former is referred to as Karyogamy and later as Plasmogamy. In fungi group, Basidiomycetes and Ascomycetes, the karyogamy is delayed and takes place just before meiosis. In the stage intervening between plasmogamy and karyogamy the cells often contain two nuclei or Dikaryons (n+n) and the phase is known as dikaryophase. The life cycle of the such fungi have three phases.

Fungi group like Phycomycetes, dikaryophase is absent and fusion of the haploid gametes forms diploid cells.

Yeast is unicellular and useful economically in fermentation.
Penicillium is multicellular and used for the production of antibiotics.
questions.solution: Morels and truffles are Ascomycetes fungi, which are eaten as delicacies. Neurospora is commonly known as Drosophila of plant kingdom and is used as an experimental material in cytogenetical studies. Yeast is unicellular Ascomycetes fungi, which is used in bread and beer making. First antibiotic penicillin was obtained from fungi Penicillium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Read the following statement and find out the incorrect statement.
options: The altered understanding of the plant kingdom describes that Fungi and members of the Monera and Protista having cell walls have now been excluded from Plantae.
Cyanobacteria that are also referred to as blue green algae are not 'algae' any more
Numerical taxonomy is based on chromosome number structure and behaviour.
Chemotaxonomy that uses the chemical constituents of the plant to resolve confusions, are also used by taxonomists these days.
questions.solution: The branch of science that deals with the naming and classification of living organisms on the basis of similarities and dissimilarities. is called taxonomy. Numerical taxonomy based on old observable characteristics. It is done by using computers. Numbers and codes are assigned to those characteristics and then processing starts. In chemotaxonomy, classification is done on the basis of chemicals that organisms possess. In cytotaxonomy, the classification of living organisms is done on the basis of their cellular structure especially chromosome number, meiotic behavior, and its structure. So the incorrect statement is C.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The Sporozoa are _____ having an infective ____ stage in their life cycle. An example of Sporozoa is the genus______, which causes malaria.
questions.solution: The sporozoans are parasitic protozoans which have an infectious spore-bearing stage in their life cycle. These organisms usually have alternate stages of asexual and sexual reproduction. During the infective stage, these parasites form cysts which divide and produce sporozoites that enter the host's cells and cause infection in them. An example of Sporozoa is the malarial parasite, Plasmodium which causes malaria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the given statements that describe an infectious particle.

(i) It was discovered by T.O. Diener and was found to be smaller than viruses.
(ii) It causes potato spindle tuber disease.
(iii) It is a free RNA particle which lacks the protein coat.
(iv) It has low molecular weight RNA as genetic material.

Which of the following organism is characterized by the above characteristics?
questions.solution: Viroids are small, circular RNA molecules without a protein coat, and they consist only of nucleic acid( RNA). They require other helper viruses to establish an infection. The smallest viroid identified is small cytoplasmic RNA. It causes potato spindle tuber disease and they are smaller than viruses.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Golgi apparatus is absent in
questions.solution: The Golgi body or the Golgi apparatus is a complex organelle present in the eukaryotic cell and is involved in transporting, modifying and secretion. The blue-green algae or the cyanobacteria are prokaryotic and therefore devoid of the Golgi complex. Yeast, liver cells and higher plants have eukaryotic cells and show the presence of the Golgi bodies in them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Virion is a _____.
questions.solution:
Virus is an infectious agent having a genetic material enclosed by an organic material that can replicate inside a host organism. Viruses are known to infect all forms of living organisms.

A fully assembled virus that has not infected any host cell is called virion. It is a complete functional virus that has the capacity to infect host cell. Extracellular viruses are also called virion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a 5-kingdom classification system, the kingdom that includes the phototrophs, chemotrophs, and heterotrophs, is ______.
questions.solution: The five-kingdom classification proposed by R.H.Whittaker consisted of Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia. This classification was based on differentiating features like structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, phylogenetic relationships, and reproduction. Photautotrophs like blue-green algae were included in the kingdom Plantae, but in this classification has brought together all the prokaryotic organisms under the kingdom Monera, which also includes the heterotrophic bacteria like E. coli or pathogenic bacterias, and chemotrophic bacterias like Nitrosomonas, suplur-utilizing bacteria etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A slide under a microscope shows the following features:

(i) Unicellularity (ii) Well defined nucleus

(iii) Biflagellate-one flagellum lying longitudinally and the other transversely

What would you identify it as?
questions.solution: Dinoflagellates are unicellular protists, also known as marine planktons which make the sea appear like red tides due to its rapid multiplication. They have characteristics of both plants and animals and are organisms bearing two dissimilar flagella, one lying longitudinally and other transversely. They are considered to be algae but show a presence of well- defined nucleus which makes its placement controversial.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Dikaryon condition is not seen in:
questions.solution: Dikaryon is a condition wherein two nuclei per cell is found. This condition is seen in fungi like ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, whereas in other fungi, the fusion of haploid cells results in the formation of diploid cells immediately. Mucor is an example of Phycomycetes where asexual reproduction takes place by motile or non-motile spores and a zygospore is formed when two gametes fuse.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding Euglenoids and select the INCORRECT ones.

(i) These are mostly freshwater organisms found in stagnant water.
(ii) Their body is covered by a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.
(iii) They are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight but become heterotrophs in the absence of sunlight.
(iv) They usually possess two flagella, one long and one short.
(v) Euglenoids are multicellular ciliate protists.
questions.solution: Euglenoids are unicellular freshwater organisms with two flagella (one long one short) belonging to the kingdom Protista and are found in stagnant water. These organisms instead of a cell wall possess a protein-rich layer called pellicle, which helps to make their body flexible. They can act as autotrophs in presence of sunlight as well as heterotrophs in absence of it.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and select the option which CORRECTLY identifies the INCORRECT ones.

(i) Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by viroids.
(ii) Viruses cause diseases like common cold, herpes and AIDS.
(iii) Mycoplasma is prokaryotic organisms that completely lack a cell wall.
(iv) In Ascomycetes, the asexual spores are conidia produced endogenously on the special mycelium called conidiophores
questions.solution: Ascomycetes are fungi which have asexual spores called conidia which are produced exogenously on the mycelium called conidiophores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The smallest living cell is:
questions.solution: The Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen. Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Lichen indicate
options: air pollution due to its sensitivity to $CO.$
air pollution due to& its sensitivity to SO_{2}.
questions.solution: Lichens are a symbiotic association of the algae (phycobiont) and fungi (mycobiont). The algal partner produces food and the fungal partner provides protection to the algae. The fungi also help in absorption of minerals and water. Lichens generally do not grow in polluted areas, hence they are good indicators of pollution due $S{O}_{2}$. Air pollutants dissolved in rainwater, especially $S{O}_{2}$ (sulphur dioxide) can damage lichens.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is an edible fungus?
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Many members of Ascomycetes like morels and truffles are edible and are considered delicacies.& The fructifications of certain fungi are used as nutritious and delicious food e.g., Agaricus bisporus and A. campestris (mushrooms).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify A, B, C and D parts in this diagram of bacteriophage.
options: A - Head, B - Sheath, C - Collar, D - Tail fibres
A - Head, B - Collar, C - Sheath, D - Tail fibres
A - Head, B - Collar, C - Tail fibres, D - Sheath
A - Head, B - Sheath, C - Tail fibres, D - Collar
questions.solution:
Head is the capsular region init the genetic material is present, Tail fibre is 6 in number, it is a part of the tail.

Collar represents the junction of head and tail. This T2 bacteriophage has 2 different structures due to which it can be called a binal virus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect match from the following.
questions.solution: Archaebacteria are special since they live in some of the most harsh habitats such as extreme salty areas (halophiles), hot springs (thermoacidophiles) and marshy areas (methanogens). Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions. Methanogens are present in the gut of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes and they are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of these animals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following combination of characters is correct for slime moulds?
options: Parasitic, plasmodium without walls, spores dispersed by air currents
Saprophytic, plasmodium with walls, spores dispersed by water
Parasitic, plasmodium without walls, spores dispersed by water
Saprophytic, plasmodium without walls, spores dispersed by air currents
questions.solution: Slime moulds are saprophytes found in the kingdom Protista. These saprophytes under suitable conditions form aggregates called plasmodium without walls, which grows and spreads to several feet. When the conditions are not favourable, these organisms differentiate and form spores with true walls, resistant and are dispersed by air currents.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not applicable to viruses?
options: The virus replicates in a bacterial host.
The protein coat of a virus does not enter the host cell.
The genetic material is DNA or RNA.
The virus replicates autonomously in the absence of a host.
questions.solution: The virus is an obligate intracellular parasite and they cannot survive outside the living host cell. They are connecting link between the living and non-living. They lacks cellular organization thus can replicate only inside other living host cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the INCORRECT statement.
options: Most plant viruses are RNA viruses.
Prions possess only nucleoid and no proteins.
questions.solution: Viruses are microscopic particles that can reproduce inside a living cell that serves as a host. Viruses contain protein and genetic material like living things. Protein coat is also known as a capsid. Prions are proteinaceous agents that contain only protein and no nucleic acid.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is false?
options: TMV has a double-stranded RNA molecule.
Most plant viruses are RNA viruses.
The bacteriophage has a double-stranded DNA molecule.
Most animal viruses lack ssDNA and can have dsDNA as their genetic material.
questions.solution: TMV has single stranded RNA as its genetic material. Most plant virus generally have single stranded RNA as its genetic material. Bacteriophages generally have ds DNA as its genetic material. ssDNA is present only in few bacteriophages as their genetic material.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by:
questions.solution: Potato spindle tuber diseases is caused by viroid which are also smallest pathogens. These are small ss RNA which are not surrounded by any protein coat. They causes diseases only in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The fungi form fruiting bodies in which __________ division occurs, leading to formation of __________ spores
questions.solution: The fruiting bodies posses diploid spore mother cell, which follows meiosis (the reductional division) and produce haploid spores. The fruiting body is the reproductive structure of fungi which is clearly visible.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A group of fungi with septate mycelium and sexual reproduction either absent or not known is
questions.solution: In Deuteromycetes only asexual mode of reproduction is recognized, with the help of asexual spores called conidia hence they are also known as imperfect fungi. The members of this class when showing the sexual stages are moved to Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes. Except for Phycomycetes which has aseptate and coenocytic mycelium, other classes have branch and septate mycelium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these statements is false?
options: All prokaryotes classified under kingdom Monera have a cell wall.
All viroids have single-stranded RNA as the genetic material.
All prions don't have nucleic acid as their genetic material.
Unicellular plants have been place in kingdom Protista by Whittaker.
questions.solution: The Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen. Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants. Viroids are smaller than viruses and cause potato spindle tuber disease. It was found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid. The RNA of the viroid was of low molecular weight. In modern medicine certain infectious neurological diseases were found to be transmitted by an agent consisting of abnormally folded protein. The agent was similar in size to viruses. These agents were called prions. The most notable diseases caused by prions are bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly called mad cow disease in cattle. Unicellular plants or algae like Euglena and diatoms are classified under kingdom Protista by Whittaker. They were not included in the plant kingdom due to its members being multicellular entirely, while Monerans are prokaryotic in nature.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
After extracting an organism, the scientist listed out the below features about it:

(i) smaller than a virus,
(ii) its nucleic acid had ribose as sugar, and
(iii) lacks a protein coat.

Which of the following diseases is likely to be produced by it?
questions.solution: Potato spindle tuber disease affects the potato plant where the tubers are malformed and stunts the growth of the plant. This disease is caused by viroids which are smaller than virus and without any capsid covering of protein. It is basically a free floating single strand RNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Some bacteria oxidize various inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites, and ammonia and use the released energy for their ATP production? These bacteria are called
questions.solution: Nitrifying bacteria are included as chemosynthetic autotrophs. These bacteria firstly convert ammonia into nitrite and then nitrites are converted into nitrates. In both these processes some energy is liberated which is used for the production of ATP and organic food. Archaebacteia are chemoheterotrophs. Photosynthetic autotrophs use energy of sunlight for production of organic food. Heterotrophs cannot synthesize their own food, they depend on other organisms for food substances.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Agaricus, Alternaria and Aspergillus are genera of fungi which are included in three different classes. The respective order of these classes will be:
questions.solution: Agaricus is commonly called mushroom and all mushrooms are included in class basidiomycetes becaused their spores are called basidium/basidia. Alternaria is member of class deuteromycetes which include imperfect fungi because their only asexual stage is known. Aspergillus is member of class Ascomycetes, they have spores called ascus/asci.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find out the correctly matched option of the causative agent and their disease.
questions.solution: In modern medicine certain infectious neurological diseases were found to be transmitted by an agent consisting of abnormally folded protein. These agents were called prions. They cause bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly called mad cow disease in cattle. Citrus canker disease is caused by bacteria Xanthomonas citri. Cr-Jacob disease (CJD) in humans is also caused by prions. Small pox disease is caused by virus Variolla.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Term genome/nucleoid can be used for:
questions.solution: In prokaryotic cells, the nucleus is in primitive form. In this nucleus nuclear membrane and histone proteins are absent, so the nucleus is present in scattered form. This nucleus is called the incipient nucleus/nucleoid/genophore. Bacteria, mycoplasma, archaebacteria, and cyanobacteria (Blue-green algae) all are prokaryotes with primitive nucleus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Most of the euglenoids live in running fresh water while Dinoflagellates are mostly marine.
Euglenoids carry same pigments as that of higher plants
Amoeboid protozoans live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil
Marine amoeboids have silica shells on their surface
questions.solution: Euglenoids are members of the kingdom Protista. They live in stagnant freshwater. They show mixotrophic nutrition i.e. autotrophic as well as heterotrophic nutrition. In the presence of sunlight, they are autotrophic (having photosynthetic pigments similar to higher plants) while in absence of sunlight they are heterotrophic and show predation. Dinoflagellates are mostly marine members.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: For phycomycetes class of fungus, incorrect statement is
options: their mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic
the fusion of gametes results in the formation of zygospore.
modes of asexual reproduction are motile aplanospores and non-motile zoospores
Parasitic fungus Albugo produces white spots on mustard leaves.
questions.solution: Members of class Phycomycetes are also called algal fungi. In these members, asexual reproduction takes place by non-motile aplanospores and motile zoospores. Phycomycetes is the only class of fungi in which septa are absent so their mycelium becomes coenocytic (multinucleated). Sexual reproduction takes place by the fusion of gametes due to which diploid zygospore is formed. Albugo is parasitic fungi of mustard leaves.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statement is not correct for Viroids?
options: Causes potato spindle tuber disease and tobacco mosaic disease
In 1971, TO. Diener discovered these agents
Viroid was found to be a free RNA, it lacked the protein coat
RNA of viroid was of low molecular weight
questions.solution: Viroids are infectious agents that were discovered by T.O. Diener in $1971$. They are smaller than viruses and are found to be in the form of free RNA (without protein coat). Their molecular weight is comparatively low. They cause potato spindle tuber disease. Tobacco mosaic disease is caused by a virus named as Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bacteria may reproduce by
options: a sort of sexual reproduction by adopting a primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacterium to the other.
questions.solution: The single-celled bacterium reproduces by binary fission where it divides into two identical daughter cells. This process of fission begins when the DNA of the bacteria replicates and divides into two. When the conditions are not suitable, some bacteria produce spores and undergo asexual reproduction. These unicellular organisms also reproduce by transferring DNA which can be either floating in the environment (transformation), when the DNA moves from one bacterium to another through a conjugation tube between them by the process of conjugation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plastids are not found in
questions.solution: Plastids a double membrane organelles responsible for manufacturing and storing food in plant cells and few other eukaryotic organisms. These structures bear some specific pigments that are used in the process of photosynthesis and impart specific colors to the plants. They are not found in prokaryotes like bacteria and blue-green algae and fungi which are heterotrophic eukaryotes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Soap box-like overlapping shells are found in the cell walls of
questions.solution: Diatoms are a group of photosynthesizing algae (chrysophytes) that are found in freshwater as well as in marine waters. Diatoms have soapboxes like overlapping thin shells found in the cell wall. These walls are resistant to destruction as they are made of silica, which is also known as a frustule. Due to this characteristic feature of diatoms, the accumulation of their cell wall deposits is known as "diatomaceous earth".

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct combination of characters regarding slime molds is
options: parasitic, plasmodium with true walls, spores dispersed by air currents
parasitic, plasmodium without walls, spores dispersed by water
saprophytic, plasmodium without walls, spores dispersed by water
saprophytic, plasmodium without walls, spores dispersed by air currents
questions.solution: Slime molds are saprophytic protists, this feature is similar to fungus so they are also called fungus-like Protists. Under favorable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet. During adverse conditions, this plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. They are highly resistant and survive for many years, even under adverse conditions. Their spores are dispersed by air currents.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Primitive bacteria living in salty areas are called:
questions.solution: It is a group of archaebacteria, whose plasma membrane is single lipid bilayer, halophiles are heterotrophic bacteria which can tolerate high salty condition. Thermoacidophiles can tolerate acidic and high temperature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the correct sequence of events, with respect to the fungal sexual reproductive cycle.
questions.solution: In fungi vegetative, asexual, and sexual all three types of reproduction take place. The sexual reproduction takes place with the help of some spores like oospores, ascospores and basidiospores. Their sexual cycle is conducted mainly in three steps - $\left(a.\right)$~Plasmogamay: Fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes $\left(b.\right)$ Karyogamy: Fusion of two nuclei $\left(c.\right)$ Meiosis: Zygote undergoes meiosis and forms haploid spores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bacteria on its outer layer contains
questions.solution: On the outer layer as a cell envelop the bacteria consists of tightly bound three-layered structure i.e., the outermost glycocalyx followed by the cell wall then the plasma membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the scientists present in columns I with their contribution in column II, and choose the correct combination from the options given.
&
& Column I & Column II
& (Scientists) & (Contribution)
a. Ivanowsky 1. Contagium vivum fluidum
b. Pasteur 2. Crystallization of viruses
c. Beijerinck 3. Discovery of viruses
d. Stanley 4. Term virus
questions.solution: The term virus means venom or poisonous fluid, this term was given by Pasteur. D.J. Ivanowsky discovered certain microbes as a causal organism of the mosaic disease of tobacco, which is smaller than bacteria and can pass through bacteria-proof filters. M.W. Beijerinck told that the extract of the infected tobacco plants could cause infection in healthy plants and called the fluid as "contagium vivum fluidum" (infectious living fluid). W.M. Stanley crystallized them and these crystals were mainly consisting of proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Late blight of potato is caused by:
questions.solution: Late blight of potato is caused by Phytophthora infestans, it is a Phycomycetes fungus. This disease is also the cause of Ireland's famine.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: VAM is
questions.solution: In the case of endomycorrhizal fungal hyphae are found in cells of the cortex. In certain plants, the hyphae penetrate the cortical cells to form vesicles or arbuscles called VAM. Vesicular arbuscular mycorrhiza (VAM).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Extension of plasma membrane in prokaryotic cell is:
questions.solution: In prokaryotes, the cell membrane is infolded into small projection known as mesosomes. These are infoldings that increase the surface area of the membrane for attachment of respiratory chain complex, helps in DNA replication and separation of replicated DNA, and septa formation during cell division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All viruses
questions.solution: Viruses are infectious agents that survive only inside the living cells (host body), they need a host for replication and can have either DNA or RNA as the genetic material which replicates. These microorganisms do not have their energy and are therefore known as obligate parasites that use the energy of the host for its survival. The virus has either DNA or RNA as genetic material but never both together.& All viruses contain protein. Only enveloped viruses are susceptible to lipid solvents.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The type of organisms found in the kingdom Protista are:
questions.solution: Protists are eukaryotic organisms (having a well-defined nucleus and a nuclear membrane surrounding the nucleus). The members of this kingdom are single-celled organisms who may be autotrophic, heterotrophic or parasitic. Chrysophytes, Euglenoids, Dinoflagellates, Slime moulds and Protozoans all are the members of this kingdom which are unicellular eukaryotic organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All of the following statements are correct for blue green algae, except
options: they have chlorophyll - a, which is also found in higher plants.
they may be filamentous, colonial, or unicellular.
they have heterocysts which are clear cells without chlorophyll.
they are connecting link between plants and animals.
questions.solution: Cyanobacteria have autotrophic nutrition and can perform photosynthesis with the help of chlorophyll-a which is similar in green plants. They may be unicellular, colonial, or filamentous forms. Nitrogen fixation in cyanobacteria mainly occurs in specialized cells called heterocysts. Heterocysts are large-sized, pale-colored, non-motile, mucilage free thick-walled cells that are impermeable to oxygen. Euglena is the connecting link between plants and animals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the correct statement about the protist given& in the diagram below.&
options: These microscopic organisms float passively in water currents and are found in both marine and freshwater environments.
These protists are generally biflagellates, of which one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates.
These biflagellate protists are autotrophic in the sunlight and heterotrophic in its absence.
Their cell wall& has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface and deposits of such is known as diatomaceous earth.
questions.solution:
The given diagram is that of a dinoflagellate.
These organisms are mostly marine and photosynthetic. They appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells. The cell wall has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface. Most of them have two flagella; one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates. Very often, red dinoflagellates (Example: Gonyaulax) undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides). Toxins released by such large numbers may even kill other marine animals such as fishes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Whittaker's system of classification implies that unicellular eukaryotes are primarily precursors of the
questions.solution: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by RH Whittaker in 1969. This system was classified based on body organization, cell structure, mode of nutrition, and reproduction. This classification has helped to categorize the organisms together which were placed in different kingdoms in earlier classification. All the unicellular eukaryotic organisms have been placed under the kingdom Protista and prokaryotic organisms are grouped under Monera.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The major drawback of the two-kingdom classification system was that it did not distinguish between
questions.solution: The Two Kingdom system of classification with Plantae and Animalia kingdoms was developed that included all plants and animals respectively. This system did not distinguish between the eukaryotes and prokaryotes, unicellular and multicellular organisms and photosynthetic (green algae) and non-photosynthetic (fungi) organisms. Classification of organisms into plants and animals was easily done and was easy to understand, but, a large number of organisms did not fall into either category. Hence the two kingdom classification used for a long time was found inadequate.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In nature, a symbiotic association is found between an algae and a fungus. Which of the following can be regarded as the correct property for this association?
options: Lichens are fast growing organisms that live for a short period
The algal component is called mycobiont and fungal component is called phycobiont
They are pioneers of vegetation on rocks.
questions.solution: Lichens are symbiotic associations between algae and fungi. The autotrophic algal component is called phycobiont and the heterotrophic fungal component is called as mycobiont. Algae prepare food for fungi and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner. Lichens are very good pollution indicators - they do not grow in polluted areas and in cities. Lichens are pioneers in the xerosere type of ecological succession on barren rocks.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In lichens, the phycobiont and mycobiont are _______________ and ______________, respectively.
questions.solution: Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi. The algal component is known as phycobiont and fungal component as mycobiont, which are autotrophic and heterotrophic, respectively. Algae prepare food for fungi and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Causative agents of sleeping sickness and malaria are included respectively in which classes of protozoa?
questions.solution: Sleeping sickness disease is caused by Trypanosoma which is included in class flagellated protozoa. Malaria disease is caused by Plasmodium which is included in class sporozoan. All members of this class are parasite and these are devoid of locomotory organs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The causative agent for mad cow disease is:
questions.solution: Prions: In modern medicine certain infectious neurological diseases were found to be transmitted by an agent consisting of abnormally folded protein. The agent was similar in size to viruses. These agents were called prions. The most notable diseases caused by prions are bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly called mad cow disease in cattle and its analogous variant Cr–Jacob disease (CJD) in humans.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct, according to Ernst Mayr's concept of species?
options: Species is a genetically open system
All organisms of a population have a common gene pool
Two species are not reproductively isolated
questions.solution: According to Ernst Mayr (also known as The Darwin of the twentieth century), all organisms of a population have the common gene pool.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following properties in the options given below& will be shown by all of the following organisms?
& Trypanosoma, Noctiluca, Monocystis, and Giardia
questions.solution: Protista is the kingdom of unicellular eukaryotes. The protists include heterotrophs, autotrophs and some organisms that can vary their nutritional mode depending upon the environmental conditions. Protists occur in freshwater, saltwater, soil and as symbionts within other organisms.& Trypanosoma, Noctiluca, Monocystis& and& Giardia& are all unicellular protists.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Asexual reproduction takes place by zoospores or by aplanospores in:
questions.solution:
Members of phycomycetes are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in the moist and damp places or as obligate parasites on plants. The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic. Asexual reproduction takes place by zoospores (motile) or by aplanospores (non-motile). These spores are endogenously produced in sporangium. A zygospore is formed by fusion of two gametes. These gametes are similar in morphology (isogamous) or dissimilar (anisogamous or oogamous). Some common
examples are Mucor, Rhizopus, (the bread mould mentioned earlier) and Albugo (the parasitic fungi

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which group of fungi, conidia are produced exogenously on conidiophores?
questions.solution: The asexual spores that are found on the external surface of the spore-producing structures or cells (conidiophores) which produces it are known as conidia. This kind of reproduction is seen in the ascomycetes group of fungi also known as sac fungi which are mostly multicellular saprophytic decomposers a parasitic. Few examples of this fungi are Penicillium, Aspergillus, Claviceps and Neurospora.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Lichens are indicators of pollution as:
options: They grow more on polluted areas
They are not found in non-polluted areas
They do not grow in polluted areas
questions.solution: Lichens: Lichens are symbiotic associations, i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi. The algal component is known as phycobiont and fungal component as mycobiont, which is autotrophic and heterotrophic, respectively. Algae prepare food for fungi and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner. Lichens are very good pollution indicators – they do not grow in polluted areas. They cannot grow in the atmosphere having a high concentration of oxides of sulphur.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: CJD caused by prion proteins is seen in
questions.solution: Prions: In modern medicine, certain infectious neurological diseases were found to be transmitted by an agent consisting of an abnormally folded protein. The agent was similar in size to viruses. These agents were called prions. The most notable diseases caused by prions are bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly called mad cow disease in cattle and its analogous variant Cr–Jacob disease (CJD) in humans.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bacteria that live in most harsh habitats are
questions.solution: Archae groups are similar to eukaryotic organisms because they lack a part of the cell wall and they are similar to bacteria in a way that their genetic material is spread throughout the cell. Thus, they are a blend of bacteria and eukaryotes. Archae can live only in areas without oxygen. A remarkable trait of archaebacterial is their ability to survive in extreme environments which include very salty, acidic, harsh and hot surroundings. Due to this trait, it was also concluded that they were a very ancient form of life to evolve on earth.
